title: Why developers and enterprises choose the Precip Weather API
summary: Comparing the Precip Weather API with IBM Environmental Intelligence Suite (The Weather Company APIs): 1 km observed rainfall history, benchmarked 60-minute nowcasts and 10-day forecasts, and modern REST, GIS, embed, and MCP integrations.
body_markdown:
If you are building software for agriculture, construction, insurance, utilities, logistics, or outdoor operations, adding a weather API looks simple on day one. Every provider accepts a latitude and longitude and returns a clean JSON array of hourly rain, temperature, and wind.


The trouble starts a few weeks after launch, when a customer calls to ask why your app says their job site got` 0.02"` of rain last night when their trench is under two inches of water.


The bug isn’t in your code. It is in what most weather APIs return when you query a coordinate.


## The “history” problem


When you ask a typical weather API for yesterday’s rainfall at a coordinate, it almost always returns one of two things:


1. **The nearest airport weather station (ASOS/METAR):** Great if your user’s field or job site happens to sit on an airport runway. In practice, the nearest station is often 10 to 25 miles away. A summer thunderstorm can dump two inches on a site and miss the airport completely.
2. **A stored model forecast or coarse reanalysis (ERA5, GFS, or HRRR):** Many APIs stitch together the first few hours of old numerical weather prediction runs or a 9 to 30 km reanalysis grid and label the endpoint` /history` . If the model predicted rain three miles to the east, that miss is permanently baked into your “historical” data.


When we tested the NOAA High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) model against independent rain gauges across the U.S., Precip’s 1 km radar-and-gauge observation pipeline had **60% lower error** on rainfall totals and **275% better rainfall detection** ([see the history benchmark](https://precip.ai/our-precipitation-data#history-benchmark) ).

The[Precip Weather API](https://precip.ai/developers) serves all three from a single coordinate and tile stack, and we benchmark every horizon in public against independent NOAA stations:

**Next 60 minutes** **1 km** , 1-min & 5-min steps In-house radar nowcast trained on gauge-calibrated ground truth **#1 in 37 of 38 live tests** vs. Apple Weather, Google Weather, Tomorrow.io, and Rainbow.ai ([benchmark](https://precip.ai/nowcast-benchmark) )

When you request a time range that crosses` now` , Precip returns measured observations up to the current hour and seamlessly continues with the nowcast and blended forecast.


## Soil, snowpack, and water


Standard weather APIs stop at 2-meter air temperature, wind, and precipitation. For field operations, what happens once water hits the ground is just as important:


- **Root-zone soil moisture and soil temperature (` 0–10 cm` and` 10–40 cm` ):** Query both absolute volumetric moisture and relative moisture (scaled from` 0%` wilting point to` 100%` saturation using 30-meter POLARIS soil hydraulics), plus hourly soil temperature for planting and agronomic models.
- **Surface ponding and saturation depth:** Identify standing water and how deep a crew can trench before hitting saturated soil.
- **Snowfall totals and snowpack depth:** Separate fresh liquid-equivalent snowfall (at 1 km) from actual snow depth on the ground (via NOAA NOHRSC SNODAS and CaLDAS).

### 1. 1 km vs. 4 km matters on the ground


A 4 km grid cell covers 16 square kilometers (nearly 4,000 acres). A 1 km Precip cell covers 1 square kilometer (about 247 acres). When a narrow convective band drops two inches of rain on a subdivision, a solar farm, or a row-crop field, a 4 km grid averages that downpour with the dry miles around it.


And while The Weather Company leans on crowdsourced Weather Underground personal weather stations (which frequently suffer from wind undercatch, roof heating, or clogged tipping buckets), Precip trains its 1 km radar refinement on quality-controlled federal and climate reference networks and continuously refines the record as verified gauge reports arrive.


### 2. No SKU maze


Legacy enterprise weather contracts split basic observations, short-term radar nowcasts, extended hourly forecasts, and soil/agronomic layers into separate add-on packages. When a product team wants to add soil moisture or a 60-minute rain chart to a customer dashboard, it triggers a contract renegotiation. With Precip, one integration gives your team the entire stack from the sky to the root zone.


### 3. Public benchmarks instead of black-box claims


Enterprise buyers should not have to take “proprietary AI forecast” on faith. Precip publishes live, station-level verification against NOAA’s U.S. Climate Reference Network, 2,200+ ASOS airport stations, and NOAA’s 2.54 km URMA analysis on[/nowcast-benchmark](https://precip.ai/nowcast-benchmark) and[/forecast-benchmark](https://precip.ai/forecast-benchmark) , and we publish our 5-minute CONUS nowcast runs to a public Zarr v3 archive 24 hours later so your data science team can audit our numbers on your own coordinates.


## Five ways to integrate


Different engineering teams need different surfaces. Every commercial Precip API key works across all five:


### 1. REST Point & Multi-Point API (` JSON` ,` GeoJSON` ,` CSV` )


Query` /api/v1/hourly` ,` /api/v1/daily` ,` /api/v1/minutely` , or rolling windows (` /api/v1/last-24` ,` /api/v1/last-48` ) for one coordinate or a batch of sites:


```text
curl   -G   "https://api.precip.ai/api/v1/hourly"   \
-d   "latitude=42.2808"   \
-d   "longitude=-83.7430"   \
-d   "start=2026-10-01"   \
-d   "end=2026-10-07"   \
-d   "format=json"   \
-H   "Authorization: Bearer   $PRECIP_API_KEY  "


```


### 2. Web Map Tiles (` XYZ` ) & Esri ArcGIS` ImageServer`


Drop` EPSG:3857` XYZ raster tiles straight into Mapbox GL, MapLibre, Leaflet, or OpenLayers, or connect our time-enabled Esri` ImageServer` URLs (` /api/v1/map/{layer}/ImageServer` ) directly into ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and QGIS with built-in legend and point-identify support.


### 3. Hosted Embeddable UI (` /embed/location` )


If your team wants to ship a complete weather dashboard inside a SaaS product this afternoon without building charts and map layers from scratch, drop in a single` <iframe>` :


```text
<  iframe
src  =  "https://api.precip.ai/embed/location?lat=42.2808&lon=-83.7430&units=imperial&key=YOUR_API_KEY"
style  =  "width: 100%; height: 460px; border: 0; border-radius: 12px;"
title  =  "Precip Weather"
></  iframe  >


```


See how[Verdi shipped Verdi Weather](https://precip.ai/blog/verdi-weather/) to their irrigation customers using the embed UI.


### 4. Remote MCP Server for AI Assistants & Agents


Building an LLM agent or internal copilot? Connect any Model Context Protocol client to` https://api.precip.ai/mcp` with OAuth or a Bearer API key to give your agent 20 structured weather and location tools.


### 5. Zero-Signup Pay-Per-Use (` x402` )


For autonomous agents, serverless scripts, or one-off backfills, call` https://api.precip.ai/x402/...` or` https://api.precip.ai/mcp-x402` and pay per lookup in USDC via the HTTP` 402 Payment Required` header, with no account or subscription required.
